feed.title: Proposal: OP_STARK_VERIFY - Native STARK Proof Verification in Bitcoin Script

entry.title: Proposal: OP_STARK_VERIFY - Native STARK Proof Verification in Bitcoin Script
entry.summary:
The exploration of cryptographic protocols such as [STIR](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/390) and [WHIR](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1586.pdf) reflects a significant interest in enhancing the efficiency of cryptographic proofs, particularly concerning their size and the speed at which they can be verified. These protocols are part of a broader category known as sum-check protocols, which are central to various applications in cryptography and computational complexity theory. Their development and optimization could potentially lead to more streamlined and faster cryptographic operations.
Concerns regarding the adoption of specific zero-knowledge (ZK) protocols within systems like Bitcoin are noteworthy, especially given the hesitance to integrate an opcode tied to a ZK protocol that is not universally optimal. The ideal scenario would involve a basic, lightweight primitive that does not depend on any specific protocol but still offers the necessary functionalities to be widely adopted. An example of such a primitive is the concept of [batch polynomial evaluation](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/448), which presents a promising avenue due to its general applicability and independence from particular cryptographic frameworks. This approach might facilitate easier consensus within the Bitcoin community, as it avoids the pitfalls of committing to a single, possibly suboptimal cryptographic method.
Overall, the ongoing research into these protocols and primitives suggests a proactive approach towards creating more efficient, scalable, and versatile cryptographic tools. Such advancements could significantly impact the practical deployment of cryptographic protocols across various technologies, including blockchain.
